text:
Anya: Heads-up — ran a focused econ pass on the new 20B family (fp16, bf16, int8 mixed) for the chat/assistant workload. Quick notes and asking for recommendations for GTN and product routing.
Devon: Nice. TL;DR numbers? :eyes:
Anya: Summary: int8-mixed reduces per-token GPU cost ~42% vs fp16, but we see a 1.8% BLEU/ROUGE-style drop on our conversational QA eval set and a 3.1% uptick in hallucination rate on longer context prompts. Tail latency (p95) improves ~8ms. Evidence linked: https://internal.eval/reports/20b-mix-2028
Sam: Can you paste the unit econ calc you used? want to sanity-check.
Anya: Sure — used simple cost per token basis using measured tokens/sec on our p4d pools and hourly GPU cost. Code snippet:
```
# rough calc
tokens_per_sec = 1100   # measured for int8-mixed
tokens_per_min = tokens_per_sec * 60
cost_per_hour = 6.5      # $/GPU-hour (blended)
cost_per_token = (cost_per_hour / 3600) / tokens_per_sec
# annualized per 1M tokens:
cost_per_1M = cost_per_token * 1e6
```
Anya: Results: fp16 ~ $9.6 / 1M tokens, int8-mixed ~ $5.6 / 1M tokens, bf16 roughly $8.9 / 1M.
Linh: So ~42% savings is real. But that 1.8% quality drop — how is it distributed? a few hard families or broad regression?
Anya: Mostly concentrated on multi-step reasoning prompts and math-heavy QAs. Single-turn chit-chat and instruction following are fine. Scorecard attached in the report — worst buckets are: chained-reasoning, tabular extraction, and numeric accuracy.
Devon: For GTN we should consider route-based thresholds. Product can tolerate small quality hits on low-SLA/low-revenue tenant flows (user summaries, low-risk features). But for billing-sensitive or trust features (invoices, legal), stick to fp16.
Maria: For commercial messaging to customers, we need clear guidance: e.g., "Default to int8-mixed for non-critical routes; enable fp16 for verified/document/fin flows." Also estimate monthly $ savings for a median customer using 50M tokens/mo.
Sam: Quick calc for 50M tokens/mo: int8 cost = 5.6 * 50 = $280; fp16 cost = 9.6 * 50 = $480 => $200/mo savings (42%). Annualized ~$2.4k. Good callout for GTN.
EVAL-Bot: Automated eval summary: 20B-int8-mix vs 20B-fp16
- Avg loss delta: +0.12
- QA exact match delta: -1.7%
- Hallucination delta: +3.1% on long context (>2048 tokens)
- Perplexity shift: +0.6
- Latency p95 improvement: 7.9ms
Link: https://internal.eval/reports/20b-mix-2028 (artifact)
Linh: Thoughts on mitigation? We could soft-fallback: first attempt int8, if safety/consistency checks fail (low confidence score, high repetition penalty) reissue on fp16. That keeps most requests cheap and absorbs regressions.
Devon: Agree. Also recommend a configurable per-customer "quality floor" toggle exposed in Dedicated/Private so platform teams can opt-in.
Anya: One more: quant noise seems concentrated in numeric formatting (dates, currency) and table parsing. We can add targeted post-processors (regex fixes, format validators) to recover ~60% of those errors cheaply.
Maria: For GTN & product pitch: propose a small playbook:
- Default routing: int8-mixed for all non-SLA routes
- Critical routes: fp16 pinned
- Soft-fallback: deterministic checks + automatic reissue
- Feature parity: add numeric-format validators
- Savings callout: example customer saves ~42% -> include $/token + 50M token example
Sam: Suggest adding A/B canary for 2 weeks targeting 5% traffic to evaluate live regressions; instrument delta metrics (errors, reissues, user-reported complaints).
Anya: I created a canary config draft in the repo (link in thread). Also added required eval prompt-suite for chained reasoning to monitor regressions.
Devon: Final ask: Can eng-ml produce an ops-friendly short doc (1-pager) with the above routing rules + fallback logic + quick rollback steps? Product will attach it to GTN pitch.
Linh: I can draft the 1-pager. Also will add the validator prototypes and plan a 5% canary.
Maria: I'll prepare the GTN slide with cost/benefit using Sam's numbers and a risk appendix.
Anya: Sweet. If no objections, we'll land int8-mixed as default for non-critical routes and roll the canary early next week. :rocket:
Devon: +1
Sam: +1
EVAL-Bot: Canary scheduled (config-id: canary-20b-mix-2028) — monitoring hooks enabled.
